cases.name: Ashleigh Porshay Berry Moore
cases.about: She was a member of Second African Baptist Church. Ashleigh attended DeRenne Middle School and was in the Magnet Program. She was a member of the Georgia Childrens Book Award Academic Quiz Bowl Team and was also on the basketball team. She had scored 800 on the S.A.Ts and had been accepted in the Duke University Honors Program for this summer.
cases.caseStatus: CASE DISMISSED; POLICE / D.A. MISHANDLED CASE
cases.narrative: On 5/14/2003, following a massive community manhunt, a fisherman found her body hidden in the undergrowth along the Savannah River. An autopsy confirmed she had been raped and strangled.

cases.name: Susan "Sue" Elizabeth Hall Burnette
cases.about: Her obituary said, "She was a devoted US Army wife over his 36 year career, a staunch Atlanta Braves fan, and a loving mother, grandmother, and aunt. She had a passion for helping others especially US Army spouses. She was an avid craftsman, designing and creating numerous Sue Burnette Original "America Rocks" crafts for her many US Army and civilian friends and family. She was a dedicated member of the Ft. Stewart Spousal Club and Southbridge Bunco group."

cases.name: Madalyn "Maddy" Coulter
cases.about: She was a veteran and former Nine Line Apparel employee. “She did her time in the military, she did it well, she was a trooper. She loved her country. She did everything that was expected of her and even more, and she broke some boundaries, and she was proud of that,” her sister Jackie and brother-in-law George Miller said. They say they’ll remember her joy for life. “She was amazing, she was funny, she was very funny. She loved life, she was smiling, always smiling. It didn’t matter the situation. She would make light of it.”
cases.narrative: On 7/12/2022, a Savannah Police officer found her dead inside a vehicle in the rear parking lot of the DoubleTree Hotel on Yvette J. Hagins Drive.
